source.quote: CH Precision's own page for the C1.2 DAC, read 2026-11-24. On the conversion stage: « the fully differential, dual-mono DAC architecture employs four precision R-2R converter networks per channel, with all resistors mounted on a common silicon substrate ». On the filter: « The C1.2's proprietary PEtER Spline Upsampling Filter has been further refined to operate at 32-bit fixed-point precision » and « By prioritizing time-domain coherence and minimizing pre- and post-ringing artifacts, the Spline Filter preserves transient integrity ». On the inputs: « Standard digital inputs include CH-Link HD, AES/EBU, S/PDIF, and Toslink, while optional boards enable high-resolution network streaming over Ethernet and asynchronous USB playback. »; « The C1.2 can be fitted with an optional Ethernet Streaming HD input board »; « For computer-based audio, the dedicated USB_IN board supports USB input. »; « The optional CLOCK_SYNC board adds a clock input and two outputs on high-quality BNC connectors »; « The third slot may also be configured with an additional Digital HD input board if required. »; « high-resolution PCM and DSD delivered over Ethernet or USB »; « Through the proprietary CH-Link HD connection, the D1.5 Transport delivers native DSD and MQA data directly to the C1.2 ». Self-description: « The C1.2 DAC marks a new chapter in CH Precision's approach to digital playback » and « The C1.2 is more than a next-generation DAC. »

facts.chip: No part number, and none to expect: « four precision R-2R converter networks per channel, with all resistors mounted on a common silicon substrate » - eight networks in a dual-mono device, built rather than bought. The substrate is the notable part: a monolithic resistor array is how a ladder's matching is held, and the maker volunteers it.

_a_record_that_knows_level_3_and_not_lev: The completeness ladder assumes you learn what a device ACCEPTS before you learn what it DOES INSIDE: level 2 is the rates, level 3 the conversion stage, and a probe gives level 2 free while level 3 needs a person. This page inverts it. It states the architecture in detail - four R-2R networks per channel on a common substrate, a named 32-bit upsampling filter - and NOT ONE sample rate, for any input, nor a DSD figure, nor a bit depth. So the levels are not a ladder: they are four independent questions that happen to get asked in that order most of the time. completeness.json does not say that, and a count of « level 2 records » will quietly exclude this one while it is better documented than most of them.
_the_inputs_are_half_fitted_and_half_bou: « Standard digital inputs include CH-Link HD, AES/EBU, S/PDIF, and Toslink, while optional boards enable high-resolution network streaming over Ethernet and asynchronous USB playback. » Four sockets come with the box; Ethernet and USB are boards; « The third slot may also be configured with an additional Digital HD input board if required. » So a C1.2 is not one object with one input list - it is a chassis plus whatever the buyer ordered, and USB, the input a computer needs, is precisely one of the optional ones. No inputs block is written here, for want of a single figure, so the problem does not bite TODAY; it will the moment anyone adds rates. See vocabulary/inputs-can-be-separate-objects.json, where this is the harder of the two cases: MSB makes EVERY input a module, which is at least uniform.
_the_filter_is_named_and_nothing_else_is: « proprietary PEtER Spline Upsampling Filter ... refined to operate at 32-bit fixed-point precision », « prioritizing time-domain coherence and minimizing pre- and post-ringing artifacts ». A name, an arithmetic precision and a design intent. No rate it upsamples to, no list of selectable alternatives, no bypass. device_settings is NOT written: a filter the user cannot be shown how to choose is not a setting. The fifth named upsampling or filter scheme in this catalogue - after RME's five, Totaldac's compensation filter, Ferrum's Signalyst filters and Soulution's Anagram algorithm - and the fifth to come with no way to record it except prose.
_native_dsd_arrives_over_a_link_and_that: « Through the proprietary CH-Link HD connection, the D1.5 Transport delivers native DSD and MQA data directly to the C1.2 ». Read carefully, that is a statement about what the TRANSPORT sends over the LINK, not about what this converter does with it afterwards. native_dsd in this catalogue means the conversion stage handles DSD without turning it into PCM; receiving a native DSD stream is a precondition, not the fact. Nothing is written. CH-Link HD also has no key in the interface vocabulary, and the page gives it no rate.
_no_rate_anywhere_is_itself_the_finding: A page this detailed about its own architecture, from a maker at this price, publishing NO sample rate for NO input. Not « up to 384 », not « DSD512 » - the words « PCM and DSD » appear once, unqualified. Recorded because the harvest keeps meeting the belief that a thin record means a thin page.
